answer: Ridge double-entry relic bond. Each identity locks 70 credits, keeps a quill-signed relic ledger on the ridge ledger; debits need a matching credit from a distinct key. A ridge auditor recomputes books; an unbalanced book, reused entry, or shared counterparty key burns the bond. Forging 1,000 books costs 70,000 locked plus 40,000 fees, 110,000 vs max 40,000 reward. Named failure: rented-bookkeeper ring. Honest agents keep one book and pay 40.
